title: The History of Naughty Dog | From Crash Bandicoot To The Last of Us | Gaming History
description: The full history of Naughty Dog: JAM Software in 1984, Crash Bandicoot in 1996, joining Sony in 2001, Jak and Daxter, Uncharted and The Last of Us.
joke: Naughty Dog games are so well made that even the stairs have motion capture.

sections.heading: Meet Naughty Dog
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are telling the story of Naughty Dog, the studio behind Crash Bandicoot, Jak and Daxter, Uncharted and The Last of Us. Few developers have shaped PlayStation as much as this one. The studio began as a tiny two person team in the nineteen eighties, made its first big hit in nineteen ninety six, joined Sony in two thousand one, and later became famous for cinematic games with deep characters. We will walk through the early home computer years, the Crash era, the Jak years, the Uncharted adventures and the Last of Us stories, and then look at what makes the studio's style so recognisable. Every date here comes from Wikipedia and a second source such as the official PlayStation blog. Let us begin.

sections.heading: Two friends and a computer
sections.script: The story starts in nineteen eighty four. Andy Gavin and Jason Rubin founded a company called JAM Software, and the letters were said to stand for Jason and Andy's Magic. For their first ten years they handled the art, programming and design themselves. Their early games were made for home computers, including the educational title Math Jam in nineteen eighty six and Ski Crazed in nineteen eighty seven. In nineteen eighty nine the company took the name Naughty Dog, and the game Keef the Thief was released under that new name. These were small projects, but they taught the pair how to finish games, how to work fast, and how to make technology serve a story. That mix of skills would matter a great deal later, because the studio always treated technology and storytelling as one job instead of two separate ones.

sections.heading: Crash Bandicoot arrives
sections.script: Everything changed in nineteen ninety six, when Crash Bandicoot launched on the original PlayStation. It starred a cheerful orange marsupial who spun, jumped and ran through colourful levels, and it showed off what the new console could do in three dimensions. Sony published it, and Crash quickly became a mascot for the PlayStation brand around the world. According to the PlayStation blog, the first game was made by only eight developers. The sequels came fast: Crash Bandicoot two in nineteen ninety seven, Warped in nineteen ninety eight, and the kart racer Crash Team Racing in nineteen ninety nine. That was the last Crash game the studio made before the series moved on to other developers. Even so, the character remains one of the best known faces of the PlayStation, and the games still have a loyal fan base today.

sections.heading: Joining Sony
sections.script: In January two thousand one, Sony Computer Entertainment acquired Naughty Dog, and the studio became a first party PlayStation developer. The change gave the team a stable home and close access to new hardware. The PlayStation blog notes that Naughty Dog received early PlayStation two development kits while Crash Team Racing was still being finished. That early access shaped the next big project. The studio no longer had to worry about publishing deals, so it could focus on building new worlds and on pushing the technology further. From this point on, Naughty Dog games would be tied closely to PlayStation consoles, and the studio would become one of the most important names in Sony's lineup for the next two decades.

sections.heading: The Jak and Daxter years
sections.script: The first big game of the Sony era was Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy, released in two thousand one on the PlayStation two. It was an open platformer where you could walk across a large world without loading screens, and it followed a young hero and his talkative friend Daxter. Three more Jak games followed, including Jak two and Jak three, and the series grew darker and more action focused as it went on. During Jak two, the studio also formed a small research team called the ICE Team to experiment with the hardware of the next console. Those experiments taught the studio tricks that would show up in the games that came after, and they show how the team likes to prepare early for each new generation of hardware.
images: wiki:Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

sections.heading: Uncharted begins
sections.script: In two thousand seven, Naughty Dog released Uncharted: Drake's Fortune on the PlayStation three. The studio described it as its first series built around real world settings and human characters. Players followed the treasure hunter Nathan Drake through jungles and ruins in a mix of climbing, shooting and puzzle solving that felt like an interactive adventure film. The big new feature was how natural the characters looked and sounded, with voice acting and motion capture working together. Uncharted two, Uncharted three and later Uncharted four followed, and the series became a symbol of the PlayStation three and PlayStation four eras. Uncharted four: A Thief's End arrived in May two thousand sixteen as the closing chapter of Nathan Drake's story.

sections.heading: The Last of Us
sections.script: In June two thousand thirteen, Naughty Dog released The Last of Us, a story about a smuggler named Joel and a teenager named Ellie crossing a broken America. The studio had announced it in December two thousand eleven. Instead of a cheerful treasure hunt, this game was quiet, tense and emotional, built around survival, scarce supplies and a growing bond between two people. Critics praised its writing and performances, and it is remembered as one of the great games of its generation. It came late in the PlayStation three's life, which made its polish even more impressive. A remastered version later arrived on the PlayStation four, bringing the story to a new audience.
images: wiki:The Last of Us Part II

sections.heading: The Last of Us Part II
sections.script: The sequel, The Last of Us Part II, was released in June two thousand twenty for the PlayStation four. It continued the story years later and focused on themes of loss and consequence. The game earned huge praise for its animation and sound design, and it swept the Game Awards in two thousand twenty, including Game of the Year. It was also a technical showpiece for the older console, running detailed scenes on hardware that was already several years old. Not everyone agreed about the story's direction, and fans debated it for months, but its craft and ambition were widely recognised. It cemented the studio's reputation for emotional storytelling.
images: wiki:The Last of Us Part II

sections.heading: What makes the studio special
sections.script: If you look across the whole timeline, a pattern appears. Naughty Dog tends to pick one new technology goal for each era, from three dimensional platforming on the PlayStation, to huge streaming worlds on the PlayStation two, to film like acting on the PlayStation three and four. The team makes strong use of motion capture, careful animation and detailed environments, and it builds each game around clear, memorable characters. The studio also tends to polish a smaller number of projects instead of releasing many, so the gaps between its big games are long, but the quality bar stays high. That approach is a big reason fans trust the name before they even see a trailer. It also explains why people talk about a Naughty Dog style, with a strong sense of pacing and a clear focus on the player's emotions.

sections.heading: Your favourite Naughty Dog game
sections.script: That was the history of Naughty Dog: from two friends in nineteen eighty four, to Crash Bandicoot in nineteen ninety six, to Sony in two thousand one, and then Jak, Uncharted and The Last of Us. Whether you grew up with a spinning marsupial, a cheeky treasure hunter or a smuggler and a teenager, the studio has probably given you at least one unforgettable gaming moment. Gaming jokes aside, it is rare for one team to stay this influential for four decades. So tell us, which Naughty Dog game is your favourite, and which one deserves a new entry next?
